source.note: AC3 requires a snapshot at engage, at every transition, and at park and close. The only production path that writes those rows is the single call recordDriverUsage(ctx, it, current.Status, *req.Status, now) in workItemSet (internal/verb/workitem.go:736). No presented test goes through that path. Every verb test calls recordDriverUsage directly, and no test in internal/ or tests/ runs `story set` (or workItemSet) and then asserts a driver_usage row. Deleting that call, or moving it outside the `if transitioning` block, would leave every presented test passing. No test asserts the trigger labels either. `close` is exercised only indirectly, through the Pending assertion. `engage` and `park` (DriverTriggerEngage/DriverTriggerPark from driverUsageTrigger) are never asserted, and park changes behaviour because it is one of the two triggers that can stamp Pending. To close the gap, add one test that drives real transitions through the dispatch seam: the workItemSet verb, or runRoot `story set`. Use a stub driverSnapshotter and a session env. Take one story through an engaging entry, an ordinary transition, a park (blocked) and a terminal close. Assert one driver_usage row per transition carrying the expected delta and trigger (engage / transition / park / close). Re-issue the same `story set` and assert that no second row is written, so AC7 is also proven end to end.
